title: Direct-image and open-extension comparisons in the native Weil realization
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For each $k_0$-scheme $S$ locally of finite type, use the abelian category $\mathcal W_S$ of pro-etale Weil sheaves and its ordinary derived category $D(\mathcal W_S)$, with the actual equivariant operations of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. All maps below are over $k_0$; absolute separatedness over $k_0$ is not imposed.

(a) For composable maps $u:S\to T$ and $v:T\to H$ between these schemes, there are natural isomorphisms
$$R(vu)_*\cong Rv_*Ru_*,\qquad R(\operatorname{id}_S)_*\cong\operatorname{id}_{D(\mathcal W_S)}.$$
These are isomorphisms in the native equivariant derived categories, for total right derivation in $\mathcal W$, without any constructibility or boundedness assumption on the input.

(b) If $j:U\to S$ is a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], its equivariant sheaf extension by zero $j_!:\mathcal W_U\to\mathcal W_S$ is exact. Its termwise descent $J_j:D(\mathcal W_U)\to D(\mathcal W_S)$ carries bounded constructible cohomology to bounded constructible cohomology. For composable quasi-compact open immersions $j:U\to S$ and $i:S\to T$ there are natural equivariant isomorphisms
$$J_iJ_j\cong J_{ij},\qquad J_{\operatorname{id}_S}\cong\operatorname{id}_{D(\mathcal W_S)}.$$
Constructibility here is exactly the locally finite stratified $B_S$-module condition in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], not a convention identifying this category with fixed pairs in another derived category.
